stem: If $(1+x)^{{=n}} = c_0 + c_1x + c_2x^2 + \dots + c_{{=n}}x^{{=n}}$, find the numerical value of $c_0 + c_1 + c_2 + \dots + c_{{=n}}$.
solution: The identity $(1+x)^{{=n}} = c_0 + c_1x + \dots + c_{{=n}}x^{{=n}}$ holds for every value of $x$.
Substitute $x=1$: the right side becomes $c_0 + c_1 + \dots + c_{{=n}}$.
notes: Same skeleton as the book question, with n varied. Substitute x=1.
